Hi Alex / Acme POC team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to meet the folks who will run the evaluation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned success criteria and timeline for the 2-week POC/trial: 

Summary of goals (agreed on call):
- Validate accuracy of Redwood-generated customer support replies across three intents (billing, password reset, plan change). Target: >85% intent match and <1% hallucination on factual fields.
- Measure end-to-end latency for single-threaded conversational flows (target 300-400ms median per token generation for 512-context runs).
- Confirm integration surface: streaming responses to your chat UI + tool calling to trigger ticket creation in your internal system.

Success criteria (proposed):
1) Functional: intent accuracy >= 85% on a 200-case test set you provide.
2) Performance: 95th percentile token latency <= 800ms for expected traffic profile.
3) Operational: log/audit events visible in Console and KV cache warming reduces cost by >=10% over baseline.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): share evaluation dataset + grant sandbox access
- Week 1: integration and baseline runs (SDK integration + sample flows)
- Week 2: run evals, iterate prompts, handoff to product owners, close POC

Owners and contacts:
- Redwood sales / POC lead: Marissa Cole (me) — overall timeline, billing/terms
- Redwood engineering contact: Dev Patel — SDK, API routes, streaming and tool-calling guidance
- Acme technical lead: Alex Johnson — integration owner, provides dataset and access

Attachments: I attached a short MOP (redwood-poc-mop.pdf) and an integration checklist (integration-checklist.xlsx) that maps the items above to owners and dates.

Next steps for Acme:
1) Share the 200-case evaluation CSV by EOD Tue (please upload to the Drive link or reply with attachment).
2) Confirm sandbox access details (API key or SSO) and preferred kickoff time for the integration session this Thursday.
3) Sign the mutual action plan in DocuSign (link below) if you want formal tracking — optional.

I’ll loop Dylan and Dev into a 60-minute technical kickoff once we have the dataset.

Thanks,
Marissa

Hi Alex / team — quick tech note ahead of the kickoff: below are the recommended integration approaches and sample payloads to cover streaming + tool calling. Happy to walk through live during the session.

1) SDKs / auth
- We have official SDKs for Node and Python. For the POC we recommend Node (express) sample to minimize setup.
- Auth: sandbox API key (Bearer) — do not use production key. We’ll rotate keys per environment.

2) Streaming & chat
- Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat/stream - Use chunked transfer encoding, accept: text/event-stream for SSE and our SDK handles reconnects.
- Example (pseudo):
  const stream = client.chat.stream({ model: 'redwood-3b-opt', messages: [{role:'user', content:'...'}], max_tokens: 512 });
  stream.on('message', chunk => render(chunk));

3) Tool calling (ticket creation)
- We recommend Redwood's tool-calling interface: declare a tool in your config, Redwood will return a tool_call action with name + arguments; after receiving that, perform a POST to your ticket API and return the status to Redwood via the tool response API.
- Recommended ticket JSON schema (example):
  {
    "summary": "{{user_message_summary}}",
    "user_id": "{{user_id}}",
    "priority": "low|medium|high",
    "source": "redwood-poc",
    "metadata": {"conversation_id":"{{conversation_id}}"}
  }

4) Idempotency & retry
- Ticket creation should be idempotent: include conversation_id to avoid duplicates. If your API returns 409, return a tool result with existing ticket id.

5) Observability
- We’ll emit trace IDs and a structured audit event for each tool call to the Console. During the kickoff Dylan will show how to filter by conversation_id.

6) Security notes
- Use mutual TLS on your ticket API if available. All sandbox traffic will be over TLS and authenticated with API keys.

Sample code and Postman collection: I attached a small Node example in the Drive link and will paste the minimal snippet below the fold. Let me know if you prefer Python.

Looking forward to Thu.

—Dev
